layers.label: Orientation — what the system is and why
layers.intro: Start here if you are new. This layer answers what the system is and how it is shaped, before any detail.

entries.what: Product goals, scope, primary actors, and the big picture — read first — Read first — establishes the product's purpose, scope, and primary actors before any structural or behavioral detail.

Layer diagram, tech stack, service boundaries, and the main data flow — Read after the overview because the layer diagram, tech stack, and data flow only make sense once you know what the system is for.

layers.label: Domain model — entities, features, and stories
layers.intro: The domain vocabulary — the entities, the feature catalogue, and the user stories that everything else refers back to.

entries.what: Core data entities, their key fields, and how they relate — Read after orientation — the core data entities are the vocabulary the feature list, stories, and APIs all refer back to.
The full F### feature catalogue, each with a one-line summary — Read after the entities because each feature is described by the data it touches; this is the catalogue everything else indexes into.
US### user stories grouped by feature and actor — Read after the feature list — the stories expand each F### into concrete actor goals and acceptance intent.

layers.label: Interfaces & behavior — screens, APIs, rules, permissions
layers.intro: How the system behaves at its edges: the screens users touch, the API surface, the business rules it enforces, and who may do what.

entries.what: Inventory of every SCR### screen in the product — Read after the stories because screens are where those user goals become something the user can see and touch.
How screens connect — navigation paths and state transitions — Read after the screen list so you know the screens before tracing how navigation and state move between them.
Every API route the backend exposes, with method and path — Read after the screens because the routes are the backend surface those screens call into.
API surface grouped by resource, plus background jobs — Read after the route list — it groups the raw routes by resource and adds background jobs, giving the API its shape.
BL### background/async logic units and what triggers them — Read after the API surface because the BL### units describe the async and background logic those endpoints and jobs trigger.
Which role may perform which action (RBAC matrix) — Read after the rules — it pins down which role may perform each action the rest of the system exposes.

layers.label: Deep dives — flows, per-feature, and per-screen specs
layers.intro: Drill-downs for when you need depth on one specific flow, feature, or screen — read after the layers above give you the map.

entries.what: Per-feature deep specs — functional-spec + technical-spec per feature (see note below)
